definition: Speech Synthesis Markup Language (SSML) is an XML-based markup language for speech synthesis applications.
details: It is a recommendation of the W3C's Voice Browser Working Group. SSML is often embedded in VoiceXML scripts to drive interactive telephony systems. However, it also may be used alone, such as for creating audio books. For desktop applications, other markup languages are popular, including Apple's embedded speech commands, and Microsoft's SAPI Text to speech (TTS) markup, also an XML language. It is also used to produce sounds via Azure Cognitive Services' Text to Speech API or when writing third-party skills for Google Assistant or Amazon Alexa. SSML is based on the Java Speech Markup Language (JSML) developed by Sun Microsystems, although the current recommendation was developed mostly by speech synthesis vendors. It covers virtually all aspects of synthesis, although some areas have been left unspecified, so each vendor accepts a different variant of the language. Also, in the absence of markup, the synthesizer is expected to do its own interpretation of the text.

explainer.lead: SSML is an XML-based markup language for speech synthesis applications and a recommendation of the W3C Voice Browser Working Group. It lets developers control how synthetic speech is produced, often inside VoiceXML telephony scripts or standalone for audio books.

tiers.eli5: It's a set of tags, like instructions in a script, that tell a talking computer how to say something.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers embed SSML in VoiceXML to drive interactive telephony systems or use it alone for audio books, and it drives speech in Azure Cognitive Services' Text to Speech API and other third-party services. On desktops, alternatives such as Apple's embedded speech commands and Microsoft's SAPI TTS markup, also XML, are common.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as an XML-based markup language for speech synthesis, issued as a recommendation of the W3C Voice Browser Working Group. No formula or formal limits are given.

explainer.example: An audio book producer writes SSML markup around the text and passes it to a synthesis engine to generate the narration audio.
